repo_analysis.problem: Most resume tools either blindly rewrite with an LLM (hallucination risk) or do simple keyword stuffing (no intelligence). This project addresses the hallucination problem, metric loss problem, overfit problem (lack of generalizability), and black box problem (lack of explainability) in resume optimization.
features: Parses a resume and extracts job description requirements
Performs deterministic skill matching
Calculates an ATS score
Rewrites the resume using an LLM
Validates claims and metrics to prevent hallucinations and metric loss
Includes a truth check to catch invented claims before export
Implements regex-based metric preservation to catch dropped numbers
Provides a repair pass with targeted feedback if validation fails
Exports the optimized resume only when all safety checks pass
Utilizes a LangGraph agentic workflow for orchestration
Employs structured JSON I/O for all LLM calls
Supports loading PDF, DOCX, and TXT resume formats
Skill matching uses exact match, token stem overlap, fuzzy ratio, acronym matching, and semantic aliases
evidence: LangGraph-based resume optimization prototype with semantic skill matching, ATS scoring, metric preservation, and hallucination checks.
A compact, safety-first resume tailoring system built with LangGraph and Groq.
It parses a resume, extracts JD requirements, matches skills deterministically, rewrites the resume with an LLM, validates every claim and metric, and exports only when the output is safe.
Truth check catches invented claims before export.
Regex-based metric preservation catches dropped numbers.
Deterministic skill matching is used, without embeddings or ML models for matching.
LangGraph agentic workflow is implemented.
Structured JSON I/O for all LLM calls is used.
Features a Streamlit UI.
Exports to DOCX, PDF, TXT.
